notes: Identity independently verified from title, authors J. Kiley Hamlin and Karen Wynn, Cognitive Development 26 (2011) 30–39, and DOI 10.1016/j.cogdev.2010.09.001: all match the supplied original reference. The canonical text is an excerpt of the primary journal PDF, not a secondary report or preregistration. It contains web-extracted lines 0–281 of 416, ending mid-Experiment-2 preferential-looking result; Experiment 1 results are present. No local PDF is supplied, so rendering is unavailable. No acquisition attempted. The broad description and p.5 locator do not identify an experiment, age group, choice versus looking outcome, or within-social preference versus between-condition comparison. PDF page 5 (printed p.34) contains the end of Experiment 1 choice results and Experiment 2 methods. Several preference tests satisfy the broad description. No target can be selected independently of row order or numeric matching. Candidate evidence: Experiment 1 social-choice pooled binomial p< .01 (25 of 34); nine-month and five-month social-choice binomial tests each one-tailed p < .05 (12 of 16 and 13 of 18). The same section also prints between-condition Fisher p < .005, age comparison p > .99, and control-choice p = .058, .105, .119. Experiment 2 social-choice binomial p< .05 and between-condition Fisher p < .05; its looking-time character-by-condition interaction prints F(1, 22) = 8.21, p< .01. The looking-time planned contrast is truncated. Choice passages name binomial/Fisher tests without a numeric test statistic. These are distinct candidate tests; none is assigned. No effect-size conversion or analytic N derivation performed. All unassigned fields/sides are placeholders only.
